questions.q: Find the determinant of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 5 & 6 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$.
questions.exam: WASSCE Further Maths: Combinatorics, Sequences & Matrices
questions.subject: Further Mathematics (Elective Mathematics)

questions.q: Find the inverse of the matrix $P = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$.
questions.explain: For a $2 \times 2$ matrix $P = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}$, its inverse is $P^{-1} = \frac{1}{ad-bc} \begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}$. The determinant is $(2)(3) - (1)(5) = 6 - 5 = 1$. Swapping elements on the main diagonal and negating the others yields $\begin{pmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ -5 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$.
questions.exam: WASSCE Further Maths: Combinatorics, Sequences & Matrices
questions.subject: Further Mathematics (Elective Mathematics)

questions.q: Given that the determinant $\begin{vmatrix} 3 & x \\ 2 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = 10$, find the value of $x$.
questions.explain: The determinant of a $2 \times 2$ matrix $\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}$ is $ad - bc$. Thus, $(3)(4) - (x)(2) = 10 \Rightarrow 12 - 2x = 10$. Solving for $x$: $2x = 2 \Rightarrow x = 1$.

questions.q: Solve the simultaneous equations $2x + y = 5$ and $3x - 2y = 4$ using matrices. Which of the following matrix products gives the solution for $\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}$?
questions.explain: The system in matrix form is $\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$. To find $\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}$, multiply both sides by the inverse of $A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix}$. The determinant of $A$ is $(2)(-2) - (1)(3) = -7$. The inverse is $-\frac{1}{7} \begin{pmatrix} -2 & -1 \\ -3 & 2 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{7} \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix}$. Thus, the solution is $\frac{1}{7} \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$.

questions.q: If the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 2 \\ -1 & x \end{pmatrix}$ has no inverse (i.e., it is a singular matrix), find the value of $x$.
questions.explain: A matrix has no inverse if its determinant is zero. Det$(A) = (4)(x) - (2)(-1) = 4x + 2$. Setting the determinant to zero gives $4x + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow 4x = -2 \Rightarrow x = -\frac{2}{4} = -\frac{1}{2}$.
questions.exam: WASSCE Further Maths: Combinatorics, Sequences & Matrices
questions.subject: Further Mathematics (Elective Mathematics)

questions.q: Let matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$ and matrix $B = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$. Find the product $AB$.
questions.explain: Multiply the rows of $A$ by the columns of $B$: Element 1,1 is $1(0) + (-1)(1) = -1$. Element 1,2 is $1(2) + (-1)(-1) = 3$. Element 2,1 is $2(0) + 3(1) = 3$. Element 2,2 is $2(2) + 3(-1) = 1$. This forms the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} -1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$.

questions.q: If the determinant of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} x & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$ is equal to 5, find the value of $x$.
questions.explain: Expanding the determinant along the first column gives: $x(1 \times 4 - 3 \times 2) - 0 + 1(1 \times 3 - 2 \times 1)$. This simplifies to $x(4 - 6) + 1(3 - 2) = -2x + 1$. Setting this equal to 5, we have $-2x + 1 = 5 \Rightarrow -2x = 4 \Rightarrow x = -2$.

questions.q: A linear transformation $T$ maps the point $(x, y)$ to $(2x+y, 3x-y)$. Find the matrix representing $T$.
questions.explain: The linear transformation mapping $(x, y)$ to a new point $(x', y')$ can be written in matrix form as $\begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix} = M \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}$. Since $x' = 2x + 1y$ and $y' = 3x - 1y$, the matrix $M$ simply takes the coefficients of $x$ and $y$ as its rows: $\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$.

questions.q: If $2 \begin{pmatrix} x \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$, find the value of $x + y$.
questions.explain: We can expand the matrix equation into two simultaneous linear equations. First row: $2(x) - 4 = 6 \Rightarrow 2x = 10 \Rightarrow x = 5$. Second row: $2(3) - y = 5 \Rightarrow 6 - y = 5 \Rightarrow y = 1$. Therefore, $x + y = 5 + 1 = 6$.

questions.q: For what value of $a$ is the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} a & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$ a singular matrix?
questions.explain: A singular matrix is a matrix whose determinant is equal to 0. Det = $a(4) - (3)(2) = 4a - 6$. Setting this to 0 yields $4a - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow 4a = 6 \Rightarrow a = 1.5$.

questions.q: To solve the simultaneous equations $2x + 3y = 8$ and $4x - y = 2$ using matrices, one finds the determinant of the coefficient matrix. What is its value?
questions.explain: The coefficient matrix for the given system of linear equations is $\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 4 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$. Its determinant is calculated as $(2)(-1) - (3)(4) = -2 - 12 = -14$.
